name: Ben Samuels
subject: Restricting abortions is a national security risk
body:
The United States military is struggling to recruit and retain qualified servicemembers. Banning abortions will only make matters worse.

| |
---|---|---
| | | Forwarded this email? [Subscribe here](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.nzSsbWeJT6uzPAPYL_R4PcAIXqv0zesFopoq3W4tV2M?) for more
---
Politics is full of universal truths, axioms, and unquestioned orthodoxy. We're here to take a closer look at some of that.
Welcome to **Not Quite Right ...** Where we break down unchallenged assumptions.
* * *
# [Restricting abortions is a national security risk](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=147795884&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ3Nzk1ODg0LCJpYXQiOjE3MjQzMzI2NTQsImV4cCI6MTcyNjkyNDY1NCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.SYj5xHJede8CuM8oYP26rjrd0uRaViGMB7jaZQZ1VWE)
### The United States military is struggling to recruit and retain qualified servicemembers. Banning abortions will only make matters worse.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels) and [Julie Roland](https://substack.com/@jyrola)
---
| Aug 22
---
| [](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)| | [](https://substack.com/@jyrola)
---|---|---
---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvYmVuc2FtdWVscy9wL3Jlc3RyaWN0aW5nLWFib3J0aW9ucy1pcy1hLW5hdGlvbmFsLXNlY3VyaXR5LXJpc2s_.hKlbViCpoaCJDQEbGeNPLadogNHPJna-nkjYYHN2qr4?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/bensamuels/p/restricting-abortions-is-a-national-security-risk?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store)
---
_I 'm thrilled to be joined by Navy Lieutenant [Julie "Jinx" Roland](https://substack.com/redirect/5fae3a14-33f1-4add-96fd-2769b075fa56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). LT Roland is a Naval Aviator who has deployed to the South China Sea and the Persian Gulf flying helicopters. She is also a 3L at the University of San Diego School of Law and the director of the San Diego Chapter of the [Truman National Security Project](https://substack.com/redirect/ad54b915-844d-4252-8c36-54c0ad52d859?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This article reflects LT Roland's personal views and does not represent the views of the United States Navy._
* * *
The United States military has a recruiting problem.
Staffing shortages are not limited to the military, of course. Other public sector jobs--from [teachers](https://substack.com/redirect/fe9338b2-e66c-41de-a840-686160457ed7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to [police](https://substack.com/redirect/c1e744d2-3b3e-4504-93f5-a80e86c36921?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--are struggling to hire too.
Within our armed forces, however, this is a more persistent problem. In fact, military enlistments have [been in decline for 40 years](https://substack.com/redirect/7168011b-bb23-4cc3-a703-7e7c4ad99b04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).1 It doesn't help that, as [Army Chief of Staff James McConville puts it](https://substack.com/redirect/9edbf9d8-f346-4858-b1b6-8eaf959d2f92?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "only 23% of Americans are qualified to serve." But when the numbers are already against us, we should recognize the need to recruit from every corner of American society, and to retain who we've got.
The solution? Women.2
The problem? Women [don't want to join](https://substack.com/redirect/3cdab14a-88f2-42c0-afd0-3046437a98e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and they [don't want to stay](https://substack.com/redirect/2e371f11-ad25-4db0-9159-35253d515d7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
For women already in the military, the [separation rate is 28% higher](https://substack.com/redirect/061e3d30-27c1-4d95-a478-c8e73a02719f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than men, largely attributed to [sexual assault, family planning, and childcare](https://substack.com/redirect/061d6dd3-b911-4d2e-bd6d-ba753f18322b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In the wake of _Dobbs,_ taking away abortion access compounds these issues while creating new ones.
When we talk about abortion access--[on the ballot in Missouri](https://substack.com/redirect/26740022-7286-4db4-8a92-86f5f4ba8d58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [other states](https://substack.com/redirect/d13fef86-e6a6-49c5-baf5-9c597dfc7a1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--it's usually framed as an issue of healthcare or an issue of equality. We believe that too. But here is what's **Not Quite Right** ... When the issue of abortion stands to drive away qualified servicemembers, it becomes an issue of readiness.
Fewer women in a military that's stretched too thin means a force less equipped to keep Americans safe. And that makes restricting abortion access a threat to our national security.
[Subscribe now](https://substack.com/redirect/d6edc35e-ad0c-4483-aae8-5a436da4ab24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### **Issues facing women in the military**
Our military has always, and likely will always, skew male. This isn't unique to America; outside of countries with compulsory military service,3 nowhere in the world are [women coming even close to comprising a majority of servicemembers](https://substack.com/redirect/d63e4916-8137-410f-9b5d-3f1b5ace7f4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
But in our view, **parity isn 't the inherent goal. Readiness is. **
Understanding why women are leaving--and aren't joining--the military is a critical part of addressing readiness. As long as there are qualified women who could be serving yet are choosing not to, we will remain undermanned.
[Lawmakers know it](https://substack.com/redirect/781efac7-9710-4992-80dd-c0d3e734241a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The military knows it too. In 2018, the Navy's chief of personnel, Vice Admiral Robert Burke, said of women: "That's where the talent is... We're very aggressively going after them." Yet while the [number of women in our armed forces has substantially increased since the '70s](https://substack.com/redirect/77d6d2d7-f6b4-471e-b176-dd1d1a82cd71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [it hasn't actually changed much since 2000](https://substack.com/redirect/23e8eccc-9281-4541-9de0-04d72b15c198?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In fact, in the Air Force, a higher percentage of enlistees were female in 1995 than are today.
What's going on?
The integration of women into the military has been slow going.
Though women have been able to serve [since the Truman Administration](https://substack.com/redirect/ec6529d4-4375-4e3b-b44c-3efc4ede3dcf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),4 there were roles [closed off to women until 2015](https://substack.com/redirect/c5f5eec0-9a8b-41f3-a502-12fd2d6ceff2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Today, only [16% of enlisted servicemembers and 18% of officers are women](https://substack.com/redirect/77d6d2d7-f6b4-471e-b176-dd1d1a82cd71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Even if those percentages seem promising, they don't tell the whole story: a poor retention rate means that even with more women joining at the lower ranks, they are lacking representative leadership at the top.5
It was not until 2022 that a woman led a branch of our military, when Admiral Linda Fagan [took over command of the Coast Guard](https://substack.com/redirect/3f8222a3-b6e5-4793-9e1a-b8010a051ae2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). When there are so few senior female leaders, there will be understandable--but avoidable--blind spots regarding the issues facing women.
Therefore, it is hardly a surprise that issues inherently tied to gender, like [sexual assault, family planning, and childcare](https://substack.com/redirect/061d6dd3-b911-4d2e-bd6d-ba753f18322b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), are three of the most common reasons women leave the military.
### **The blind spots**
[Nearly one in four](https://substack.com/redirect/04c663e3-60f9-4280-977a-74abebef90ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) female servicemembers report having been sexually assaulted, making [women in the military more likely to be raped by a fellow servicemember than killed in action](https://substack.com/redirect/398c68c4-0937-4e34-b20c-3d8b99255a35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).6 Decades of efforts to ["halt rape and other sex crimes in the ranks" have not accomplished the mission](https://substack.com/redirect/54358b68-ae21-4cbb-8a64-978a32e7c68d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
In the face of a recruiting drought, when polled, [28% of young people pointed to sexual assault](https://substack.com/redirect/1dcafb6f-8dec-4430-a0f3-dcc3f7e30f8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as a reason they wouldn't want to enlist. Sexual assault statistics understandably affect female retention while dissuading potential recruits (of both genders).
The military is also a challenging and at times inhospitable place for mothers and pregnant servicemembers. Take [this account from Marine Corps veteran Joanna Sweatt](https://substack.com/redirect/958fcfa0-e77e-4bfc-a93d-0776a4873063?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> I had my first child at 18. At the time, I was a dependent of my father, who was fully retired from the Air Force. Even as a teen mom, I was treated with nothing but respect throughout the process.
> Baby No. 2 came during my second year in the Marine Corps at the age of 20, and the experience couldn't have been more different. Even though I was married, my choice to remain pregnant after birth control failed was disrespected by my command and peers, who ridiculed me and made me feel inadequate as a Marine. In the naval hospital, my birthing experience was procedural and traumatic. As an active member of the Marine Corps, I was respected less and treated worse than when I was 18.
Many women also leave the military because of childcare constraints. The few military policies designed to help new parents are [difficult to navigate and inconsistently implemented](https://substack.com/redirect/72e5a1cb-4457-41f4-b0ed-d5b23795f245?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), there is insufficient childcare relative to demand, and there are [thousands of military brats on waitlists for childcare](https://substack.com/redirect/792e059b-4392-49d4-878c-ffc4aa56b68e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). To quote Major Erin Williams from that article, "Childcare is the only thing that has made me consider leaving military service."7
Accessing affordable childcare--the burdens of which fall disproportionately on women, [in the military](https://substack.com/redirect/64d25905-4829-4aea-9bd6-7267922b1ca4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and out--is an obstacle to recruiting women too. What mother wants to join an organization she already knows can't offer the affordable childcare she needs?
In 2020, a [Government Accountability Office report](https://substack.com/redirect/061d6dd3-b911-4d2e-bd6d-ba753f18322b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) noted that military leadership was neither understanding nor supportive of family needs. In the face of such glaring issues, the findings of the report are damning.
When military leadership appears so myopic in addressing the issues that have a greater impact on female servicemembers, it is frankly surprising that even [8% of women and girls ages 16-21 would still consider joining the military](https://substack.com/redirect/1b5e5d6e-20a1-450f-8b44-43c422cd3bac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).8
Now, the DOD faces a new problem threatening women's health and safety, and by extension, military readiness: limited [access to reproductive healthcare](https://substack.com/redirect/dc29bb78-c9e4-4a97-952b-134f38e78dea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[Learn more about Amendment 3](https://substack.com/redirect/f7656bf3-88cf-46a1-b7e5-51c5e5863f9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### **Why abortion access matters to servicewomen **
The rights afforded to women by _Roe_ were particularly critical for women in our armed forces, who [have unplanned pregnancies at a rate](https://substack.com/redirect/f2dbd858-8a5c-4d47-9dc5-fedfcd2c633b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) nearly double that of the [general population](https://substack.com/redirect/056413c7-95f0-4219-8bb8-28534b6d0523?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Now, against an already bleak backdrop of the state of female recruitment and retention in the military, enter _Dobbs_ , which eliminates a half-century-long right to reproductive healthcare.
For young women, [abortion access is one of the most important issues](https://substack.com/redirect/d526dc81-101d-4c94-931c-fc31aef3a9cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in this election. But for young women in the military, the results of these elections may be, in many ways, even more dire. Following the _Dobbs_ decision, the health and careers of female servicemembers have been put at greater risk almost overnight, as [40% of female servicemembers now no longer have access to abortions](https://substack.com/redirect/a00e9bb5-afdb-4611-ba70-468b560c646e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) simply because they're stationed at one of the 100 military installations in states that ban them.
For now, there's nothing stopping more women from getting stationed in those states in the future. Disappointingly, Pentagon officials [have conceded that "there is not much they can do for women."](https://substack.com/redirect/e534a068-bbc7-417b-b6af-c790ab0723c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The military has historically let down rape victims, pregnant mothers, and families. Now, the military is signaling it will do next to nothing as abortion access is restricted.
Ostensibly, the military has become a workplace where women now:
1. Are more likely to be raped than their civilian counterparts.
2. Are able to be relocated against their will to a state with restricted abortion access.
3. Are offered insufficient childcare and family planning resources.
4. Are led by predominantly and disproportionately male leadership that is neither understanding nor supportive.

This reveals a dystopian reality which would understandably make any woman in the military think about getting out, and any woman considering getting in think twice.
### **How Congress hamstrings our military**
The DOD's efforts to defend against the damage of _Dobbs_ have been feeble. The best current strategy involves [shipping women to other states](https://substack.com/redirect/dc29bb78-c9e4-4a97-952b-134f38e78dea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to receive essential healthcare now unavailable locally. Though Defense Secretary Austin asked commanders not to be discriminatory or retaliatory about reproductive healthcare decisions, [women reasonably fear professional consequences](https://substack.com/redirect/f96de6d8-298f-409c-b9cc-fd8babd7b254?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as "some leaders [view] the necessary time off...as an unwanted distraction."
Traveling under the circumstances will no doubt take a personal toll too. For junior enlisted service members, a [legal abortion could cost half a month's pay](https://substack.com/redirect/f74c402c-d1d1-40a9-964b-ddeb927b68c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Overall, this strategy poses more problems than it solves.
The DOD is not oblivious to the risks _Dobbs_ presents to military readiness, but Congress has made it impossible to mitigate. Current federal law [prevents the military from publicly funding abortion services and/or performing abortions](https://substack.com/redirect/4f27fde2-0182-4c3c-b47f-3fd91778a779?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) even if the patient pays out-of-pocket, with limited exceptions. Elective abortion is [one of the safest medical procedures available](https://substack.com/redirect/f103159c-82ef-479c-8a18-ec91dfe7dea8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), about [14 times safer than childbirth](https://substack.com/redirect/6f5b58ff-0d69-4ba7-8537-a8cdd9e54ec6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But while 860,000 abortions were performed nationally in 2017 alone, [only 91 have been performed in U.S. military hospitals since 2017](https://substack.com/redirect/ef158da7-2789-4894-8480-5b41c9d58f9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
There are gaps in women's healthcare access that the military should reasonably be able--but is not allowed--to close.
Moving forward, Congress could close bases in states that restrict abortion access and only build bases in states where reproductive healthcare is codified. But there's also a simpler, less dramatic, and more sensible alternative: end the [Hyde Amendment](https://substack.com/redirect/a66b3a33-1cd1-4c31-bf05-f1a23caf8717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). With the Hyde Amendment gone, military healthcare providers could actually provide necessary healthcare at any base in the country.
Understandably, the military is reluctant to weigh in on such a hot-button issue, especially around elections. Abortion access may be perceived as too politicized for the "nonpartisan" military, but this is a disservice to its members and to the country.
### **Fighting for abortion access is not just morally right. It 's tactically strategic**
If manpower is a priority, then the military needs women. Restricting abortion access stands in the way.
The increasing number of statewide bans on abortions, combined with problems already plaguing female service members (and prospective ones), [generates an "incentive for women not to serve."](https://substack.com/redirect/f96de6d8-298f-409c-b9cc-fd8babd7b254?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When it comes to the health and safety of its minority members, the military has been historically and often horrifically slow to take action. But if the military can't provide basic protections for the health and safety of its female members, readiness _concerns_ will become a readiness _crisis_.
Restricting abortion access threatens women, but it also threatens the safety of our entire country.
Unfortunately, due to the politicization of the issue, the Department of Defense may not come to women's defense. And Congressional action may take too long. Which means the American public is on the front lines for this one.
So, when you vote to [restore abortion access](https://substack.com/redirect/f7656bf3-88cf-46a1-b7e5-51c5e5863f9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Missouri (or elsewhere), remember:
You aren't just voting for Missourians. You're voting for the airmen based at [Whiteman Air Force Base](https://substack.com/redirect/53c228bb-dd8e-493b-b665-47138e094507?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and the soldiers stationed at [Fort Leonard Wood](https://substack.com/redirect/08dcaec5-9377-4f28-965c-1ad31c3d1ce1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). You're voting for all the women who serve in our armed forces, and all the women who may want to in the future. You're voting for a stronger, healthier, and safer United States Armed Forces.
And you're voting for a stronger, healthier, and safer United States.

_Hi, it 's just Ben again. Please consider supporting [Missourians for Constitutional Freedom](https://substack.com/redirect/89609d4e-f611-4510-b1a4-c210742030d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is leading the effort to restore abortion access in Missouri._
_Feel free to share this post with someone who might learn something from it, especially if they live in states where abortion access is on the ballot. (If you 're reading this email because someone sent it to you, [please consider subscribing.](https://substack.com/redirect/a22fecfc-6760-4563-9364-fba5f450e1b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_
1
While the Marine Corps and the Space Force are meeting their recruiting goals, the Air Force, Army, and Navy--the [three largest branches](https://substack.com/redirect/e16c3a31-7e67-4cc1-84fc-1796b464e112?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--are [consistently falling short](https://substack.com/redirect/cd97223c-7ea4-4068-968a-55a64f14f8ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
2
Despite what [Tucker Carlson might tell you](https://substack.com/redirect/33728674-e54e-49f8-8d50-61f82a931429?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
3
Israel requires most women to serve, and [34% of those serving in the IDF are women](https://substack.com/redirect/95158597-3231-4660-855a-2e129d02f633?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But numbers that high are very much the exception.
4
Of course, women played a critical role in conflicts before then, particularly during WWII. Even then, they enlisted in separate branches of the military--the [Women's Army Corps](https://substack.com/redirect/b36fd134-ef42-424b-8791-1b4996ada7f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for example. And many of their contributions came on the home front because they were not serving abroad.
5
For instance, in 2016, female Navy Captains fell short of proportionally representing their female junior Sailors by 11%. Despite efforts to correct the discrepancy, the number of female [Navy Captains had increased only one percent in ten years](https://substack.com/redirect/3cdab14a-88f2-42c0-afd0-3046437a98e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). At that rate of change, it would take 110 years for upper leadership to be representative, which makes convincing women that they can progress [a tough sell](https://substack.com/redirect/781efac7-9710-4992-80dd-c0d3e734241a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Plus, until women comprise their fair share of the upper ranks, decisions will be made without proportional female perspectives.
6
As Julie has written about, the issue of rape is [particularly acute in the Marine Corps](https://substack.com/redirect/276b9ea6-3d57-48f9-bc7f-49331f572eec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): "female Marines are almost three times as likely to be victims than their Air Force counterparts."
7
Erin Williams wrote a [great LinkedIn post on this topic](https://substack.com/redirect/a538a6ca-a4f6-4271-9be3-7528a18c7379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
8
While the number of women who want to join the military has been flat since the beginning of the century, it has declined precipitously for men--especially over the last six years or so.

The DOD is not oblivious to the risks Dobbs presents to military readiness, but Congress has made it impossible to mitigate. Current federal law even if the patient pays out-of-pocket, with limited exceptions. Elective abortion is , about . But while 860,000 abortions were performed nationally in 2017 alone, . There are gaps in women's healthcare access that the military should reasonably be able--but is not allowed--to close. Moving forward, Congress could close bases in states that restrict abortion access and only build bases in states where reproductive healthcare is codified. But there's also a simpler, less dramatic, and more sensible alternative: end the . With the Hyde Amendment gone, military healthcare providers could actually provide necessary healthcare at any base in the country. Understandably, the military is reluctant to weigh in on such a hot-button issue, especially around elections. Abortion access may be perceived as too politicized for the "nonpartisan" military, but this is a disservice to its members and to the country. Fighting for abortion access is not just morally right. It 's tactically strategic If manpower is a priority, then the military needs women. Restricting abortion access stands in the way. The increasing number of statewide bans on abortions, combined with problems already plaguing female service members (and prospective ones), When it comes to the health and safety of its minority members, the military has been historically and often horrifically slow to take action. But if the military can't provide basic protections for the health and safety of its female members, readiness concerns will become a readiness crisis. Restricting abortion access threatens women, but it also threatens the safety of our entire country. Unfortunately, due to the politicization of the issue, the Department of Defense may not come to women's defense. And Congressional action may take too long. Which means the American public is on the front lines for this one. So, when you vote to in Missouri (or elsewhere), remember: You aren't just voting for Missourians. You're voting for the airmen based at and the soldiers stationed at . You're voting for all the women who serve in our armed forces, and all the women who may want to in the future. You're voting for a stronger, healthier, and safer United States Armed Forces. And you're voting for a stronger, healthier, and safer United States. Hi, it 's just Ben again. Please consider supporting , which is leading the effort to restore abortion access in Missouri. Feel free to share this post with someone who might learn something from it, especially if they live in states where abortion access is on the ballot. body:
Trump’s flying in for another visit. He’s doing events both today and tomorrow, because he knows he has to win in Arizona to have any chance at retaking the White House.
#

My convention speech is tonight, Peter. I’m working on the finishing touches right now, and I hope I make you proud.
But there’s another thing happening today, back in Arizona: Trump’s flying in for another visit. He’s doing events both today and tomorrow, because he knows he has to win in Arizona to have any chance at retaking the White House.
We can’t let him. So, I’m humbly asking you to make a contribution — $5 or anything you can afford — before then. If that’s all you need and you’re ready to chip in, please use this link:
[**https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/Trump-AZ-08-24**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-august24.kZit_I&refcode=em240822-1-160&t=1&akid=2919%2E734936%2EzZ3_eY)
Back in 2020, Arizona was one of the states that decided the Senate and the White House. Trump barely lost — just a few thousand votes decided the race. It was one of the most expensive states in the country, but we kicked Trump out of the Oval Office and sent Mark Kelly to the U.S. Senate.
In 2022, we defeated Blake Masters and won Mark a full term in the U.S. Senate. We defeated Kari Lake, too, but it was down to the wire. Every race was decided by the slimmest margin. And again, Arizona was one of the most expensive states in the entire country.
Now, in 2024, Trump’s gaze is fixed firmly on Arizona. He’s here so much I can’t even keep count anymore. Kari Lake is surging, we’re neck and neck. And I checked the numbers last night. Right now, there’s already about $12 million in advertising on the books against me in Arizona, and that number is only going to grow.
I’m hoping that tonight folks sit up and take notice — we need to win in Arizona again. But we can’t, we won’t, if we don’t raise what we need to compete. We’re budgeting out every dollar right now, and we’re falling short of our goals.
So, before my speech, before Trump’s event in Arizona, I am respectfully asking you to make a donation to my campaign.
[**Please — show that you’re one of the few who understand just how important Arizona is to our chances this year and chip in. Anything — seriously, anything — helps. Even $5 or $10.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-august24.kZit_I&refcode=em240822-1-160&t=2&akid=2919%2E734936%2EzZ3_eY)

subject: Can you believe it's been 1 year?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Debbie for Florida
body:
One year ago, we launched this campaign for U.S. Senate
| | |
---
This is a special week, friend — particularly because of today's milestone: **One year ago, we launched this campaign for U.S. Senate.**
For the last year, we've been fighting hard to reach Floridians and speak to who Rick Scott truly is: a failed leader who has put the extremist policies of Donald Trump, and his own self-interest, above all else. Floridians are catching on, as Rick Scott's approval rating is abysmally underwater.
But this was never just about Rick Scott. It's about you, the people, in Florida — and all over the nation — who deserve a true public servant looking out for your interests. Service has, and always will be, at the heart of everything I do. When I'm in the Senate, I'll fight with everything I have to move the needle on the issues that actually impact your everyday life.
And together, I know we can win and make a difference. So whether you've been on this team with me for the last 365 days, if you joined last week, or even if you joined today, I want to say this: **Thank you so much. I couldn't have come this far without you, and I can't win on Election Day without you. I'm so grateful for your grassroots support.**
This past year has been a whirlwind in all the best ways. I've toured all over Florida and spoke with so many amazing voters across our diverse, beautiful communities. I've spread our message across the airwaves, starting with Spanish ads. **And thanks to our hard work, we are statistically tied with Rick Scott in the polls.**
But now is where the real work begins. I'm the official Democratic nominee for this Senate race, and with just 74 days to go, we must fight with everything we've got to win this race — because if we do, it will virtually guarantee a Democratic Senate majority.

Photo by [Kevin Grieve](https://substack.com/redirect/3622a47a-194d-4943-8434-5456287083d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on [Unsplash](https://substack.com/redirect/0b347fb0-0569-493f-9de7-09148bbf4f95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's always intriguing to see how disconnected many of our elected officials can become from the people they pledge to serve. It's a rare occurrence to find a Republican campaigning on raising taxes and expanding government. Yet, unfortunately, many follow that path once elected. It seems that once they become part of the government machine, their perspective shifts, and the very growth of government they once opposed suddenly seems justifiable.
Local elected officials have a responsibility to manage their communities and provide the services citizens need and want. As Republicans, we expect them accomplish this and uphold the principles and policies that align with our platform and ideology.
The Mississippi Republican Party clearly states its stance on taxes in its platform:
_" Mississippi Republicans believe that people, not government, know best how to spend their own money. When people keep more of their hard-earned money, jobs and economic growth will flourish in the free market system._
_Mississippi Republicans support the reduction of the tax burden on our citizens. We believe our tax burden is too high, our tax code is too complicated, and our tax system is inefficient. We believe in the reduction of taxes to empower taxpayers, create a more competitive environment for job creation, incentivize work, entrepreneurship, and investment, and prevent the excessive growth of government. "_
Given this core belief, one would reasonably conclude that no elected official claiming to be a Republican would ever support a tax increase.
Unfortunately, that's not the case in Walnut, Mississippi. Elected officials here have proposed a tax increase. How many of these politicians ran their campaigns on a platform of raising taxes? My guess is ZERO.
This November, the Mayor and Aldermen of Walnut are asking the citizens to approve a tax increase:
_" Shall the Town of Walnut, Mississippi (the "Town"), levy and collect a special sales tax from every person, firm, or corporation operating a hotel or motel in the Town at a rate of 3% of the gross proceeds of room rentals for each such hotel or motel, and from every person, firm, or corporation operating a restaurant in the Town at a rate of 3% of the gross proceeds of the sales of the restaurant derived from retail sales of prepared food and beverages, including beer, alcoholic beverages, and non-alcoholic beverages, whether such prepared food and beverages are sold for consumption on the premises or otherwise, which shall be in addition to all of the taxes and assessments currently imposed, for the purpose of providing funds to promote, construct, finance, operate, equip, lease, and maintain existing and new parks and recreation facilities and equipment in the Town, and for related purposes."_
If you believe in the Republican ideology of lower taxes and smaller government, the only vote is a resounding NO!

subject: Before I take the stage tonight at the DNC…
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=1808%2E135344%2EP2ganf)

Friend --
Later tonight, I will be taking the stage at the Democratic National Convention.
I hope that you’ll tune in. In any case, I want to explain why this is a rare opportunity for our campaign and how it connects to Democrats’ efforts nationwide.
I will have the chance to introduce myself -- and our race -- to Democrats across the country who know how critical of a swing state Michigan is. And on the final evening of the convention, in that critical primetime window, that opportunity is magnified.
It is a night where Democrats up and down the ticket -- culminating with Vice President Harris -- will prosecute the case against Donald Trump and talk to America about what a second Trump presidency would mean for our future.
Historically, the convention is also a moment that generates a surge in enthusiasm for the Democratic candidates. This means new volunteers, a surge in the polls, and yes, grassroots donations at a scale that helps power a campaign.
The Republicans, and our opponent, certainly experienced that surge during their convention. And they will be watching to see if Democrats can match, or even exceed their efforts.
**[So I am asking: before I take the stage tonight at the Democratic National Convention, will you chip in $3 to help power our campaign here in Michigan?**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-aug24._YMjeK&refcode=em240822-1-900&t=2&akid=1808%2E135344%2EP2ganf)
I know it may seem hard to believe that $3 will make a difference in an election where so much money will be spent, but by the time you make your $3 contribution, dozens of others will have made their $3 contribution, and they’re hoping you’ll do the same.

I'm so proud to be the party that represents middle class and working families. Think about it – the top of the Democratic ticket are a couple of kids from West Point, Nebraska and Oakland, California.
One of them joined the National Guard and became a high school teacher and championship-winning football coach. The other worked at McDonald's in college and became a prosecutor who held big banks accountable when they took advantage of hardworking folks.
As a kid from Southeast Pennsylvania, who remembers putting water in my cereal when my family couldn't afford milk, who joined the Army as a way to pay for college, and graduated from West Point – I'm so proud to be a Democrat right now.

Millions of people have entered the United States illegally and now they are our responsibility here in Connecticut. **The actual cost is rising fast and the amount of money spent to care for them is shocking.**
[ DONATE](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4f7b992f-02c0-4d9e-888a-f3fb1ffd73b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/cf4651dd-3a09-4df6-b613-fae038b8fbea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Just like we broke the [energy bill crisis](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/d3bbfaf5-0ff9-495a-b226-3d232adaeef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it is time you know what illegals cost us.
While we do not have Connecticut figures - Take a lesson from our border neighbor - **New York**. Here are some frightening data points on costs for illegals in less than one year:
July, 2023 - monthly costs were $284,805,056
January, 2024, monthly costs were $662,026,525 (_**a 232 percent increase in 6 months**_)
June, 2024, monthly costs were $1,030,322,204 (_**a 362 percent increase in 12 months**_)
[](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6dc25b80-4362-4df1-94d8-eb0a20ecd7de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/3f919477-6ca6-458a-a1c1-adec75017a90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**THATS RIGHT - in less than one year or illegals has more than tripled (362 percent).**_
This cost of illegal care represents $1 billion dollars **per month - THAT IS** 5% of the total New York State budget.
There are additional costs to New York and other Cities. In the first six months of 2024 **New York City spent** 2.85 **billion** dollars on illegal aliens. New York's 2024 Budget is $106.7 Billion dollars. _**NYC is separately spending approximately 5% of its budget on illegals. AND -** They have _a cumulative three-year budget gap of $13.9 billion.
_**What does this mean for Connecticut?**_
If New York State and New York City are spending over $1.5 billion dollars per month, States Like Connecticut (_**with an amount that has not been disclosed)**_ must be spending a similar amount as a percentage of total budget.
I am sure New Yorkers would love a 5 percent savings on their tax bill and Connecticut taxpayers would rather use that for gas, groceries, school supplies or other inflation related cost increases due to bad policies of Jim Himes, Kamala Harris and Joe Biden.
**Should any state go into debt to pay for illegals? NO.**
Education is probably not included in these costs to educate children here illegally. As this is also going on in Connecticut, the average cost per student is $20,000-25,000 per student (not including special ed).
I suspect that there are similar numbers in Connecticut but no one knows. Demand Accountability - Demand Transparency.
**What is the Solution?**
Hard working tax paying Americans need leaders who believe that when our Constitution says that we are a government by the people and for the people that it means that we are a government that works for its citizens not those who violate our immigration laws. Connecticut's motto is Qui Transtulit Sustinet," (He Who Transplanted Still Sustains). Well that is for Nutmeggers - its not transplant everyone here as that is not sustainable.
It is time for a change - Send a message to Himes this November as your Acting Director of Intelligence who loves an open Border - Lets Put a Doctor in the House and Let's Close that Border.
Any support is appreciated as we have a race to win, a State to take back and a Country to Heal. Together we can get it done.

| Dear Fellow American,

I sent you this email last week because I wanted you to know just how hard we are working to defend the rule of law and transparency in government....and that we're not taking a break this summer!

Your support is what makes all our vital work possible, and [I urge you to help us with a special contribution to help us continue to meet all the challenges we are confronting.](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)

And thank you for all your help!

Sincerely,

Thank you,

Tom Fitton
President
Judicial Watch

| Dear Fellow American,

Your time is valuable, so let me get right to the point...
**Judicial Watch is fighting on more fronts than ever to expose public corruption, support the rule of law and fight for the American people's "right to know"...**
**[And at this critical point in mid-August, I am asking for you to give us your support!](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)**
**Here's why:** | [Contribute](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)
---

* **We 're pursuing our next steps in preparation for litigation **over the U.S. Secret Service's denial of multiple Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests we have made related to last month's assassination attempt on former President Trump, which resulted in the death of an innocent bystander. The Secret Service is in full cover-up mode over its _epic failure_ to protect Trump and others at the rally...and we will use every legal tool to force the release of documents the American people have a right to see!

[Contribute](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)
---
* **Last week we filed a FOIA lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)** for records of Anthony Fauci, other top officials, grantees and contractors regarding efforts to _subvert FOIA and other information requests about COVID issues_. We know that there was a systematic attempt by government bureaucrats to circumvent FOIA requests during the COVID era. We are committed to undoing this massive cover-up about government response to one of the biggest public health crises in recent years.

[Contribute](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)
---
* **We're anticipating a ruling _any day now_ on our motion for expedited appeal **in our lawsuit against **Mississippi** over its law that permits ballots to be counted up to 5 business days after Election Day. Our motion would open the door to possibly shutting down this open invitation to voter fraud before the November 5th general election. And we are also pursuing a similar lawsuit against **Illinois** and its 14-day law "extending" Election Day!

[Contribute](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)
---

We have never been more deeply involved in consequential legal battles over transparency in government and preserving honest elections...

...and that is why I am _[counting on you to help now](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=69807&L=30946&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL3RoYW5rLXlvdS0yMTYvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=aafc90fdace25a5a1871d30fa9a66413e29290f69056683c8a490d5fbaf2a4d2)_.

The American legal system is slow at times, but it works best at stripping away the efforts of corrupt politicians and secretive bureaucrats to keep "we the people" in the dark about what our government is doing....

...and the legal system and the courts are _just as critical_ in helping protect fair and honest elections from the Left's attempts to corrupt them!

Thanks to the support of our members, today Judicial Watch is the largest and most effective government watchdog group in the nation. We're always fighting for you and the rule of law!

Thank you in advance for helping us perform all this essential work.

Sincerely,

Thomas Fitton

---
Large companies have increasingly hired third-party auditors to perform daytime checks on their facilities to minimize risk associated with a host of potential violations - including violations of child labor laws.
Social compliance audits are not enforceable and typically don't catch many violations during the brief daytime hours auditors are given limited access to those factories.
Most child labor happens on the night shift to avoid detection by auditors and inspectors, multiple independent and academic studies have found.
The horrors these children and adult employees often face in manufacturing and agricultural plants were [detailed in a December 2023 article by the New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/9ef5d2a2-e6ec-49b8-ae28-58a4efdadc1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The story sent shockwaves across the companies and industries named in the article.
The New York Times article[ even won the 2024 Pulitzer Prize in Investigative Reporting](https://substack.com/redirect/462f7e86-59b1-4916-a203-8efb521884fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the reporter who wrote the piece won a $15,000 prize.
But the auditor who went on the record to bring these truths to light - the only auditor named in the piece - lost his job and is being sued for his bravery in coming forward.
Joshua Callington, the auditor who spoke to the Times, conducted thousands of social compliance audits with UL Solutions from 2017-2024.
[Click here to help Joshua](https://substack.com/redirect/1be44380-7831-4fc4-98bb-e680f24a7a4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When Callington failed a Walgreens jerky factory in Minnesota three times for child labor violations, Walgreens contacted his employer to have him removed from their account.
When Callington flagged labor issues at a Costco potato warehouse, the plant's management complained about the 21 violations he found in their facility.
The day the article was released, Callington was suspended from his job. He was eventually fired, and then sued for disclosing "trade secrets" to the Times by discussing his work.
The validity of Callington's claims were never challenged.
Callington was accused of being "overzealous" and his company implied he was "impolite" in dealing with the very companies where child labor was discovered, but never of being wrong or failing to do his job properly.
Now, he's[ struggling to raise the funds needed to retain legal services in a SLAAP suit](https://substack.com/redirect/1be44380-7831-4fc4-98bb-e680f24a7a4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that accuses him of sharing documents that contain "highly confidential business information belonging both to UL and its customers."
AKA - the proof that companies Callington named were in fact engaged in the conduct he accused them of.
The intent of the lawsuit could not be more transparent - his former employer is suing him as punishment for talking about illegal child labor practices he personally observed and reported, falsely claiming Callington should have first raised the issues within the UL system before speaking to outside parties.
"Also, without UL's knowledge or approval, Defendant further disclosed certain confidential documents and information to a New York Times reporter to assist the reporter in ultimately publishing a national article about corporate America's purported approach to social responsibility audits. The New York Times article, in turn, also disclosed UL's and the customers' internal business information."
Callington did, in fact, raise these issues within the UL chain of command - repeatedly. The issues were never addressed.
A SLAPP suit, or Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation, is a civil complaint or counterclaim filed against a person or organization that speaks out on a matter of public interest.
The purpose of a SLAPP suit is to intimidate and silence critics by forcing them into costly and time-consuming legal battles. The plaintiff typically doesn't expect to win the lawsuit, but instead wants to exhaust the critic's resources and make them stop speaking out. SLAPP suits can also discourage others from speaking out, as they might face a similar lawsuit.

body:
Hi there, it’s Tom Suozzi.
At the DNC I delivered our campaign’s message to the whole nation— and stood firmly with our next President, Kamala Harris . Here’s what I said.
My family’s story is America’s story. My father immigrated from Italy, went to college, was a navigator on a B-24 during World War II, came home, and was elected as the youngest judge in New York history at 28. What a country!
It’s painful to me that immigration has become so polarizing. The border is broken, and this year we had a bipartisan border deal. But that deal was blocked by far right extremists!
Now, we have to come together to celebrate a candidate who knows America is worth it. Who knows this nation, built by immigrants, is a rare and beautiful thing, and who joyfully accepts the challenge to secure our border, to treat people like human beings, and to move our country forward. That’s Kamala Harris!
But team, we need to make sure that Kamala Harris has a partner in Congress, and that means flipping the House! NY-03 is a must-win seat, and I’ll need your help to keep it.
So team–can you split a donation between me and Seth Moulton right now to keep me in Congress and ensure Kamala Harris has a partner to pass her agenda? [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/m23-suozzi]
We have a lot of work to do, and I need you by my side.
Let’s Fix This,
Tom Suozzi

subject: I'm really enjoying this DNC!
body:

Peter, The energy at the 2024 Democratic National Convention in Chicago is truly something to behold. From the passionate speeches to the sense of unity in the air, it’s clear that Democrats across the country are ready to fight for the future we believe in. Michelle Obama put it best the other night: “America, hope is making a comeback.” It’s a powerful reminder that, even in challenging times, our belief in a better tomorrow can carry us forward. But the work doesn’t stop there. It’s just beginning. Vice President Harris and Governor Walz left the convention to hold a rally in Milwaukee, reaching out to voters in the battleground state of Wisconsin. In other words, despite all the good vibes at the convention, we know this election will be an uphill battle down the ballot. As we channel that energy and hope from the DNC into our campaign here in Ohio, we must remember that our fight is just as important. The stakes are high, and the outcome of this election will shape the future of our community and our country. While the excitement of the convention is invigorating, it’s a reminder that we must be relentless in our efforts to win over voters and secure a victory in November. Your support is essential to keeping that momentum going. Together, we can bring the hope and energy from Chicago right here to Ohio. My campaign is full of a lot of firsts: I am a first-time candidate, I'm running to be the first woman to represent Utah in the Senate, and I'd be the first "influencer" elected to Congress. Although I wear many hats (mountaineer, activist, and dog mom to name a few), I earn my income as a full-time content creator.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/539e6878-32d5-4e55-b23d-c83e5be8fa6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This isn't an easy topic to discuss, but I've always been a person who works to shine light on issues we'd otherwise want to sweep under the rug. A large part of my income involves brand sponsorships and promoted content on social media.
Here's the problem: Outdated and vague FEC rules have severely limited my ability to do my job while I run for office. Basically, the current rules say that any post I make within 90 days of an election is a "coordinated communication," and I'd have to report it as a contribution. This is a huge issue, and it's caused brands to cancel their sponsorships with me.
I'm trying to fix this: last month, our team filed a request with the Federal Election Commission to clarify these sponsored posts as "business communications" and make them exempt from the rule. Even though I'm the _first_ , I won't be the _only_ full-time content creator to run for federal office. This clarity is important, and I'm happy to lead the charge on behalf of my field. Influencers aren't slowing down: Goldman Sachs says that this industry will be worth half a trillion by 2027.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/deca62c0-987e-414d-92bd-54bffbaaed9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And content creators are uniquely qualified to serve in Congress. We know about the risks and dangers of social media, and we can better legislate big tech on matters such as digital privacy, algorithmic transparency, troll farms and election interference and AI. To be honest, our government isn't known for understanding new technology. This rule is yet another example about why a diversity of experience is important in our government. Reelecting the same politicians over and over won't change that.
At the end of the day, this outdated rule is preventing me from working and running for office. The majority of lawmakers in Congress are millionaires, and it's a lot easier to run for office if you can take a full year off of work. If we want Congress to look more like America, we need to ensure that people from all backgrounds can run for federal office.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/fba7afbb-d3f7-4b5f-a706-f6f7b99bd4e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
People have said I don't "look like a US Senator". They've said a content creator shouldn't represent us in DC. But whenI told people about my dreams of being a ski mountaineer, I was _also_ met with skepticism. "You're too small, you're not strong enough." They told me my dreams were impossible and that I would die trying.
Then I summited Everest and Cho Oyu. I broke records and defied limits - and I'm going to do that again with this campaign for US Senate. Together, we can surmount any odds and change how this country works to make everyone better off. **[I'm hoping you'll join my climb with a contribution of any amount today by clicking this link. ](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/744a3d10-d469-4745-9653-0fea7592647a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
I really appreciate that you take the time to enjoy my content,
Caroline Gleich 🏔️
[DONATE](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/744a3d10-d469-4745-9653-0fea7592647a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
P.S. I mentioned I was a dog mom, so it's only fair if I share a photo!
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a98efe2b-77b7-49e3-8dd5-eedc31dc33cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

subject: NJEA Abuses Teacher Dues to Bankroll Shady Spiller's Gov Campaign
body:

|
---
| Peter, New Jersey teachers work hard, and many of them are struggling to provide for a family on their salaries. A portion of their salaries goes to the NJEA (New Jersey Education Association) — the state teacher’s union. Do their activities benefit the teachers who pay them? We’ll let you be the judge.
---
|
---
| Let’s break it down for you. Sean Spiller is a Democratic candidate for New Jersey Governor. He is also the president of NJEA. The NJEA has a history of finding back door channels to fund Spiller’s previous political runs with teacher dues. According to [new reporting by Politico](https://xtz223.keap-link001.com/v2/click/7382316acd8a0b456a083cd903ce1572/eJyNUEFugzAQ_IvPOAYDLeUWRVGESHOo2nNlYCWcGNuyl1Ia8fc6TZVTK-U0I-3s7MyeCYIWGquOlOQTvzhPSUQctNJK0LgxGkX7M-V5lqRJRJTUp50zoyXl-c_lm-C6lccRwdlCkLy-rDd1ddi976tDHZRWuHDjPp-Hp-Lms31eV3uyLP8awyBx-xG8PSnRjXBp1MnQCt-cCvoe0fqSsWmaVtYoibI1q9YMTMPkFSCC8xdOj4HATK0Sc2PMifGYZywuAjLpKfZA9REEFY0ZkaKhNkCaD7SBXuqOeiuVAkfjOHnMiiQL0YS1oLvfv9YwXwMu3y4ogP4=), a new group called “Working for New Jersey” is planning to spend $35 million in the Gubernatorial race. Shocker...the chair of this group is a former director of the NJEA. The NJEA stated on the record that they would be supporting groups that have - ironically - the word-for-word same stated goals as the Working for New Jersey mission statement. And they’ve already endorsed Spiller for Governor. Follow the money... The incestuous and shady nature of this relationship couldn’t be more clear. And the abuse of teacher dues for political gain by Spiller and the NJEA couldn’t be more disrespectful! Where is the transparency? Are teachers being told that the dues they are sacrificing to pay are going to fund the political career of the NJEA President? ENOUGH! This is a disgrace. If you agree, let’s get loud! Tweet (X), Instagram, or Facebook one of these! Let’s expose the corruption and collusion.
---
|
---
| **As a concerned New Jerseyan, I’m outraged at how the NJEA is quietly funneling dollars to the political campaign of President Spiller.** **Are NJ teachers aware that their hard earned dues are being shifted to NJEA President Spiller’s political campaign?** **ATTN NJEA: It’s time to tell the public how much money is being donated to political groups, which candidates are benefitting, and how teachers can opt out. Stop hiding.** **The NJEA is quietly bankrolling President Spillers campaign. Who loses? NJ teachers.**
---
|
---
| We can no longer sit on the sidelines and allow this type of behavior to continue in darkness. Common sense majority, let’s get to work making sure everyone in our community knows about this. They’re relying on secrecy. That’s why exposure is step one to holding them accountable and ultimately bringing change. In defiance and strength, Elizabeth Nader
President
Common Sense Club
---
|
---
| [Unsubscribe](https://xtz223.infusionsoft.com/app/optOut/0/4fd6eb57577aacb0/21457936/39b6b9e85bca48dd) Common Sense Club 165 Route 35 Red Bank, New Jersey 07701 United States

Vox - Project 2025: The myths and the facts [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=082224_1&amount=25]
There's been a lot of talk about the Heritage Foundation's "Project 2025", Team. It's time for the truth.
Project 2025 is a detailed and specific plan for what the next Republican president could ( or in the eyes of some, should ) do with his power, including the preparation needed to put the plan into action. Organized by the Heritage Foundation, a right-wing, dark money, inside-the-beltway, anti-voting think tank , and advised by more than 100 conservative groups, Project 2025 has put forth a 922-page list of policy recommendations, going agency by agency in the federal government.
This is not an unattainable "wish list" -- this is carefully crafted to be a list of things the next president’s appointees really can do , put together by many people who served in top posts under Trump last time and could well do so again. Basically, it’s an attempt to make the second Trump term way more organized and effective than the first.
This is a good place to mention that Project 2025 is also collecting a database of names of conservatives who have already pledged loyalty to Donald Trump and could easily take jobs in his potential second term, willing to start executing this plan on day one.
Are you ready to help us educate voters across the country about this dangerous and anti-democracy plan? Pitch in $25 or whatever you can now >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=082224_1&amount=25]
Project 2025 covers a lot of different things, but basically falls into three buckets:
➜ Expanding the power of the president. Various pieces of the plan attempt to consolidate executive branch power in the hands of the president and his political appointees and away from nonpartisan civil service employees and Congress. For example, Donald Trump himself could be directing voter suppression efforts through the Department of Justice.
➜ Long-term conservative policy priorities. Slashing regulations on businesses, especially in regards to the environment. Ending climate change mitigation efforts. Reducing programs to help the poor, like food programs or educational requirements. Eradicating civil rights protections, including access to the ballot and our ability to vote. The list goes on, but if you've heard it from a conservative politician over the last forty years, it's likely in this plan.
➜ An extreme religious agenda. Further federal restrictions on abortion access. New, possibly expansive restrictions on contraception coverage. Outlawing pornography and imprisoning members of that industry. Banning LGBTQ books in libraries. Rolling back or ending LGBTQ programs in schools.
Project 2025 would fundamentally alter just about every aspect of American life . We must make sure every American is aware of what their vote might mean and how this expansive blueprint would truly impact themselves, their friends, and their family before it is time for them to cast a ballot.
Fuel our efforts to spread the word and educate voters about these dangerous plans with $25 or more today >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=082224_1&amount=25]

Hung has sacrificed so much for our family and for our country. He spent 25 years in the U.S. Navy protecting our American Dream.

Being a military family isn’t easy, but knowing my husband was fighting for our children’s futures was all worth it. But now, our greatest enemies aren’t just abroad: they’re socialists right here who HATE our country and want to decimate your freedom.

Peter – our democracy is under threat.

Across the country, extremist politicians are passing laws that make it harder for everyday Americans – _including St. Louisans_ – to vote, spreading dangerous lies that threaten the very cornerstones of our democracy.

**These attacks on our fundamental right to vote are unacceptable, and we cannot stay silent.** In Missouri and beyond, voter ID laws and other restrictive measures are implemented with the sole purpose of keeping certain voices from being heard, particularly in marginalized communities.

name: Tammy Baldwin
subject: I’m used to being written off
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Tina Kotek
body:
|
#
---
_Hey Peter — Tina here! Senator Tammy Baldwin asked to reach out with an important message:_ I’m used to being written off, Peter. When I first ran for Congress in Wisconsin in 1997, no one thought I could win — especially when an extremely popular challenger jumped into the race. I remember huddling with one of my staffers at the time, and she said, _“Well Tammy, maybe you want to rethink what you’re doing because it’s going to be tough.”_ I looked her right in the eye and asked,_“Do you think I should wait my turn?”_ The next thing I said was this: **I believe that women have to run — especially when it’s hard — and not wait our turn. We can’t wait until we get a tap on our shoulder or we’ll never get anywhere.** I ended up winning that race and became the very first woman elected to the House of Representatives from Wisconsin. And it wouldn’t be the last time our team would make history. When I ran for U.S. Senate in 2012, an incredible team of grassroots supporters like you fought alongside me — even as some people wrote us off. You helped me become the first woman elected to the chamber from Wisconsin and the first openly gay Senator in our nation’s history. In 2018, despite being a top target for national Republicans and enduring over a year of attacks, you stood with me again, and we won. Time and again, grassroots supporters like you have helped us defy the odds. The battle to protect my seat this year will be no different, with this race being my toughest election yet. **My opponent and his Republican allies have already spent more than $26 million to buy the seat I hold, and recent polls are showing this race in a dead heat. Protecting this seat won’t be easy, but together, I know we can defy the odds once again.** **[_So, Peter, I’m humbly asking: Will you make a donation to my re-election campaign today to help me protect my battleground seat and the Democratic majority in the U.S. Senate?_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/91308247/493411015/1177417980?refcode=AU_TK_FR_FOT_GEN_AC_20240822_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTlkZjE4Ni05YjYwLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PTBsNcFIccBEq3XcJYFrdF-gRTr80A3PM0mjVv7S34E=)** _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation to Tammy Baldwin will go through immediately:_ | | [CHIP IN $10 NOW](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/91308248/493411016/1177417980?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&express_lane=true&amount=10&refcode=AU_TK_FR_FOT_GEN_AC_20240822_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTlkZjE4Ni05YjYwLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PTBsNcFIccBEq3XcJYFrdF-gRTr80A3PM0mjVv7S34E=)

clean_body: | Hey Peter — Tina here! Senator Tammy Baldwin asked to reach out with an important message: I’m used to being written off, Peter. When I first ran for Congress in Wisconsin in 1997, no one thought I could win — especially when an extremely popular challenger jumped into the race. I remember huddling with one of my staffers at the time, and she said, “Well Tammy, maybe you want to rethink what you’re doing because it’s going to be tough.” I looked her right in the eye and asked,“Do you think I should wait my turn?” The next thing I said was this: I believe that women have to run — especially when it’s hard — and not wait our turn. We can’t wait until we get a tap on our shoulder or we’ll never get anywhere. I ended up winning that race and became the very first woman elected to the House of Representatives from Wisconsin. And it wouldn’t be the last time our team would make history. When I ran for U.S. Senate in 2012, an incredible team of grassroots supporters like you fought alongside me — even as some people wrote us off. You helped me become the first woman elected to the chamber from Wisconsin and the first openly gay Senator in our nation’s history. In 2018, despite being a top target for national Republicans and enduring over a year of attacks, you stood with me again, and we won. Time and again, grassroots supporters like you have helped us defy the odds. The battle to protect my seat this year will be no different, with this race being my toughest election yet. My opponent and his Republican allies have already spent more than $26 million to buy the seat I hold, and recent polls are showing this race in a dead heat. Protecting this seat won’t be easy, but together, I know we can defy the odds once again. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation to Tammy Baldwin will go through immediately: | | = = | = = | = = Your support will make the difference, and I can’t thank you enough. I’m so glad to have you on my team. — Tammy Tina for Oregon PO Box 42307 Portland, OR 97242 | mailto:info@tinafororegon.com | Paid for by Friends of Tina Kotek

| | |
---
| Hi—

I wanted to make sure you saw Sienna's message. She recently collaborated with Evergreen to create one of four limited edition posters that illustrates our shared vision of a brighter future, which **we're gifting to anyone who starts a recurring gift of $15 or more this month.**

It's going to take all of us to make sure our new climate roadmap gets in front of as many decision-makers as possible, and supporting us with a monthly donation that we can plan ahead with is where you can have the most impact.

Read Sienna's story below, and [**make sure you can secure one, two, or all four posters (before they’re all gone soon!) by starting a monthly contribution today.**](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/2790290/87SdQ4wZ)

– Beth

\---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Sienna Gonzales
Date: Wed, Aug 14, 2024
Subject: What a clean energy future means to me |
| [](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/2790291/87SdQ4wZ) |
---|---|---
---
| Hi friend,

My name is Sienna Gonzales. I'm a queer Mexican and Chitimachan artist based in Los Angeles.

**I want to tell you a story.**

When Evergreen asked me to design this poster to illustrate one of four pillars of their core vision—one that centers a **thriving, just, inclusive clean energy future** —I started brainstorming my own vision of what that means to me. |
| [](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/2790292/87SdQ4wZ) |
---|---|---
---
| As an artist, **a clear vision is foundational to my creative process.**

I often begin with curating a mood board, gathering images that resonate with the colors, atmosphere, and composition of the piece I envision, which helps me set the tone of the work.

Following this, I engage in a brief creative writing exercise to describe the image I aim to create, which solidifies the emotional impact I want the viewer to experience.

Only after I establish this vision do I begin sketching—starting with broad, loose shapes to establish the composition. Gradually, I refine these sketches, bringing the piece into more and more focus.

When I heard about the **Evergreen Action Plan 2.0** , it felt like this monumental effort was also grounded in **a clear vision** , brought to life by thoughtful steps and refinements along the way.

And I was moved by the plan's commitment to helping our leaders build, piece-by-piece, the better, brighter future we all want and deserve.

**If you resonate with this vision like I do,**[**I hope you'll start a monthly donation of just $15 to support Evergreen's work.**](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/2790293/87SdQ4wZ) If you do, you'll get a free gift from Evergreen in return—one of four posters (including my own!) that illustrate a future that’s clean, thriving, just, and inclusive. |
---
[START A MONTHLY GIFT TO EVERGREEN](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/2790294/87SdQ4wZ)
---
---
| As someone who believes that optimism is a powerful force—one that not only captures attention but also inspires action—designing this poster was an incredibly meaningful experience for me. **A clean energy future embodies a collective commitment to the well-being of both people and the planet** , and it's an honor to think that my work might play a role in bringing us closer to that shared goal.

For a brighter future, |
---
| | |
---
### Sienna Gonzales
Artist & Illustrator
---
---
|
* * *
**P.S.** The other works in the poster series are _stunning._ [**If you start a recurring gift of $40 or more each month, you’ll automatically get all four as a gift!**](https://actnow.evergreenaction.com/s/2790295/87SdQ4wZ) |

And I stood eye-to-eye with the most dangerous dictators in the world as Trump's Secretary of State.

Because I'm afraid we have a problem. A big one.

The latest reports show they've stockpiled over $100,000,000 to defeat us in enough swing states to bring forth a COMPLETE LIBERAL TAKEOVER.

I don't tell you this lightly and I know that's not what you want to see happen to our country.

If all you can spare is ten or twenty bucks, that would be incredible. If you can afford more that's even better. I only ask that everyone give something.

### Wyoming's Primaries Wrap Up a Successful Year
| | [Andy Roth](https://substack.com/@sfcn)

---

| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1424602&post_id=148005905&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQ4MDA1OTA1LCJpYXQiOjE3MjQzNDE3MzgsImV4cCI6MTcyNjkzMzczOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0MjQ2MDIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.4Epo3_DIbLJeMAjqsbG_vgkPUM280-NRcH0r4LK59TU)
